root_cause.text: The Rust binder driver failed to properly detect oneway transaction spam because the spam detection logic in `TreeRange` was executed before the new request was inserted into the allocation tree, and `ArrayRange` completely lacked spam detection logic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that in `tree.rs`, the calculation of `oneway_spam_detected` (which calls `self.low_oneway_space(pid)`) was moved from before the tree insertion logic to after it. Additionally, in `array.rs`, the `low_oneway_space` detection helper was newly implemented, and `mod.rs` was updated to return this value instead of hardcoding `oneway_spam_detected: false` for array-based allocations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update reserve_new to return an additional boolean flag alongside the reserved size.

intent_record.how: This enables the function to return an additional boolean flag alongside the reserved size, allowing callers to receive more context about the reservation status.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce one-way transaction spam detection to prevent buffer exhaustion when available space is low.
intent_record.what: Modified `reserve_new` to return a tuple containing the offset and a boolean indicating if one-way spam was detected, and implemented the `low_oneway_space` helper method to check if a PID exceeds allocation thresholds.
intent_record.how: Enables the system to detect and flag processes that are spamming one-way transactions when the available buffer space drops below a critical threshold.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate the actual oneway_spam_detected status from array reservation instead of hardcoding it to false.
intent_record.what: Modified the `Impl::Array` match arm to capture a tuple `(offset, oneway_spam_detected)` from `array.reserve_new` and assigned the captured `oneway_spam_detected` variable to the `ReserveNewSuccess` struct field instead of hardcoding it to `false`.
intent_record.how: Enables the propagation of the actual one-way spam detection status from the underlying array reservation logic to the caller, correcting the previous behavior where it was always reported as `false`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused oneway spam detection logic to clean up the buffer reservation function.
intent_record.what: The code removes the definition of the unused local variable `oneway_spam_detected` along with its explanatory comment.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the redundant calculation and potential side-effects of calling `low_oneway_space` during buffer reservation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add one-way spam detection when available buffer space falls below 10% to protect system resources.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check to calculate `oneway_spam_detected` based on remaining space and process ID, returning it in the result tuple.
intent_record.how: Enables detection of one-way spamming when buffer space drops below 10%, preventing potential buffer exhaustion by identifying spamming processes.
